# Undra

> Undra is a Rust framework that owns everything under the pixels of native iOS, Android and web apps: domain logic, reactive state, the data layer, persistence and the dev loop. It generates idiomatic Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript from one Rust core, and the UI stays SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose and React. Not to be confused with undra.sh (Kubernetes) or undra.so.

Undra is open source (MIT OR Apache-2.0) and ships an `undra` CLI (`undra init`, `undra dev`, `undra build`, `undra bindgen`, `undra doctor`). Reads never cross the language boundary: each platform holds a mirror of the state, updated by one binary change-set per transaction.

## Docs

- [Undra documentation](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/): Guides and reference for Undra, the Rust framework for native iOS, Android and web apps: getting started, concepts, queries, ports, the CLI and the API.
- [Getting started · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/getting-started.html): Install the Undra CLI with brew, npm, curl or cargo, scaffold a project, run the live dev loop and run the app on iOS, Android and the web.
- [Core concepts · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/concepts.html): Stores, signals, computeds, transactions, change-sets and keyed lists, and why a list write costs the change and not the list.
- [Queries & mutations · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/queries.html): The data layer in the core: cached queries with staleness and dedup, retry, optimistic mutations with precise rollback, persistence and an offline queue.
- [Ports & adapters · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/ports.html): The ten standard ports, the default adapter on each platform, how to supply your own, what happens when one is missing, and the fakes for tests.
- [Workers & crash recovery · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/web.html): The web core in a Web Worker: where synchronous ports run, the worker.ports module, and restarting a trapped wasm core from its last snapshot.
- [Shipping an update · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/updates.html): Snapshots, cached queries and queued mutations across an app update: what migrates by name for free, how to write a hook, what is refused.
- [The CLI · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/cli.html): Every undra command and flag, the undra.toml project file, exit codes and how errors are reported.
- [Architecture · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/architecture.html): How Undra is built: the schema, generators, runtimes, wire format and C ABI, the threading model, diagnostics, and the twelve rules every change follows.
- [Error codes · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/errors.html): Every Undra diagnostic by code, from macros, schema validation, the runtime and the CLI: what triggers it, why, and the fix, with real messages.
- [API overview, Swift · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/api-swift.html): What Undra's generated Swift looks like: records, enums, errors, objects, stores, query handles and ports, and how the UndraRuntime package loads the core.
- [API overview, Kotlin · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/api-kotlin.html): What Undra's generated Kotlin looks like: data classes, sealed types, suspend functions, StateFlow-backed stores, query handles and ports.
- [API overview, TypeScript · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/docs/api-typescript.html): What Undra's generated TypeScript looks like: interfaces, unions, error classes, promise-returning stores with signals, React hooks and adapters.

## Reference

- [Swift reference · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/reference/swift.html): Every declaration Undra generates for Swift from the playground: types, errors, objects, stores, queries and ports, with their docs.
- [Kotlin reference · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/reference/kotlin.html): Every declaration Undra generates for Kotlin from the playground: types, errors, objects, stores, queries and ports, with their docs.
- [TypeScript reference · Undra docs](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/reference/typescript.html): Every declaration Undra generates for TypeScript from the playground: types, errors, objects, stores, queries and ports, with their docs.
- [Rust API reference](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/reference/rust/undra/index.html): rustdoc for the undra crate and the runtime, signals, query, ports, wire and meta crates it re-exports

## Roadmap

- [Undra roadmap: shipped, now, next and later](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/roadmap/): The Undra roadmap: what shipped in v1.0, what is in flight for v1.x, what is planned next and what is on the horizon. Updated with the project record.

## Blog

- [Why Undra keeps your UI native | Undra blog](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/blog/why-undra-keeps-your-ui-native/): Shared UI and shared logic are different bets. What Flutter, React Native and Compose Multiplatform trade, who should pick which, and where Undra stops.
- [Undra vs UniFFI and Crux: Rust under a native app | Undra](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/blog/undra-vs-uniffi-and-crux/): Three ways to put a Rust core under SwiftUI, Compose and React: UniFFI bindings, Crux's Elm-style core, and Undra's mirrored state. Dated and sourced.
- [Undra vs Kotlin Multiplatform for shared logic | Undra blog](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/blog/undra-vs-kotlin-multiplatform/): Undra and Kotlin Multiplatform both share logic and keep the UI native. A dated, sourced comparison: iOS, web, reads, tooling, ecosystem and team fit.
- [Reads never cross the boundary: how Undra works | Undra blog](https://shreypdev.github.io/undra/blog/reads-never-cross-the-boundary/): How Undra mirrors Rust state into SwiftUI, Compose and React: change-sets, keyed lists as recorded operations, a schema-hash gate, and what it all costs.
